_OrgDRGEdge.description:
One typed edge in an organisation-tier DRG fragment.

Mirrors the contract YAML example shape: ``source`` + ``target`` +
``relation`` (a ``Relation`` value).

``reason`` is the **author's own rationale** and nothing else. Machine
provenance lives on :class:`_ProjectedOrgDRGEdge.generated_reason`, a field
this class does not declare — so with ``extra="forbid"`` a fragment cannot
write one, and anything reaching ``reason`` came from a governance author.
That is the whole discriminator :func:`charter.offering.drg.merge
._warn_discarded_edge_rationale` needs; see that docstring for why reading
"has a reason" as "an author wrote a reason" was a defect.

allOf.description: A term is an edge endpoint only as the target of a vocabulary edge (ADR-0049 decision 4).

_OrgDRGEdge.title: _OrgDRGEdge

_OrgDRGNode.description:
One node in an organisation-tier DRG fragment.

Shape matches the contract YAML example: ``id`` + plural ``kind`` +
``title`` + optional ``body_path``. Distinct from
``charter.offering.drg.models.DRGNode`` (URN-based). The merge bridges the two
by minting URNs at merge time (handled in ``charter.drg``).
_OrgDRGNode.title: _OrgDRGNode

Relation.description:
Typed edge relations in the DRG.

Lineage vs. delegation vs. augmentation are three distinct concepts and
MUST NOT be conflated (FR-001, FR-002):

- ``SPECIALIZES_FROM`` (lineage): a profile derives from a parent,
  narrowing or extending it. This is a *static composition* relation used
  for inheritance/specialization (FR-001). A delegation is a substep's data,
  never an edge (ADR-0064 decision 11).
- ``ENHANCES`` / ``OVERRIDES`` (augmentation pair, FR-014, mission
  ``charter-ux-and-org-pack-vocabulary-01KSAF14``): a pack artifact declares
  ``enhances: <id>`` to field-merge into a built-in, or ``overrides: <id>``
  to declare a full replacement.
- ``REFINES`` (refinement, #2079): an artifact narrows or sharpens the
  applicability or meaning of the target (a parent or built-in) without
  replacing it. It is distinct from ``APPLIES`` (an action applies a
  directive/tactic) and from ``SPECIALIZES_FROM`` (static profile/artifact
  lineage): a refinement is a first-class, traversable relation, never a
  synonym for ``APPLIES``. Previously the org→DRG bridge silently downgraded
  ``refines`` to ``APPLIES`` (a dead sink); it is now preserved end-to-end.
- ``TENSION`` / ``RECONCILES_TENSION`` / ``REJECTS`` (tension
  vocabulary, ADR-0028 and ADR-0045): three distinct relations that must not be
  confused with each other or with the relations above.

  - ``TENSION`` is **symmetric and non-transitive**: two co-valid,
    co-activatable rules pull against each other, and neither is
    deprecated by the other. It is a pair class of its own, so it stands
    beside the one structural relationship of its pair (ADR-0045 decision 1).
    A pack writes at most one tension per unordered pair, with the side the
    pack owns as ``source``; when the pack owns both sides, or neither, the
    lexicographically smaller bare URN is the ``source``, so a pack may
    declare a tension between two artifacts it holds neither of. A duplicate, a
    reversed tension or a tension of an artifact with itself refuses the
    pack (ADR-0045 decision 6). It must NOT be confused with supersession --
    tension does not mean one side wins or is retired.
  - ``RECONCILES_TENSION`` is **directional**, from an artifact to one
    side of a tension pair. A pair counts as reconciled only when an
    artifact in force carries this edge to BOTH sides (ADR-0045 decision 8).
    It is never synthesized from ``TENSION`` -- it must be authored
    explicitly.
  - ``REJECTS`` is **directional**, from a good artefact to a marked
    anti-pattern/smell node (``NodeKind.ANTI_PATTERN``). Unlike
    ``TENSION`` the target is not a competing equal -- it is a
    named bad practice, not a co-valid rule -- and unlike a supersession the
    target was never a valid rule the rejecting artefact supersedes.

Each relation names the source and target kinds it may connect (ADR-0064 decision 13). ``impacts``, ``replaces`` and ``delegates_to`` are retired (slice F): a former ``replaces`` edge is an ``overrides`` edge.

description:
A loaded organisation-tier DRG fragment with provenance metadata.

One instance per configured ``charter_packs.org.packs`` entry. The loader
(:func:`load_org_pack`) produces a single fragment per pack root.
``layer_index`` (1..N) is assigned by the caller
(``charter.drg.load_org_drg``) once it knows the declaration order.
``provenance_marker`` is the fixed string ``"org"`` — every node and
edge from this fragment is tagged ``source: org:<pack_name>`` in the
resolved DRG (see ``charter.drg.merge_three_layers``).
title: OrgDRGFragment
